group.label: MCP Database Reader
group.comment:
Settings for the optional db.query tool — read-only SQL against this store's database. This is the highest-risk tool in the MCP family. It is off by default, gated by its own ACL resource (Tool: Run Read-Only SQL Query), and rejects anything that is not a single SELECT.

Even so, a read-only query can still expose customer PII, order history, admin account rows, and configuration values. Treat "who may enable this" and "which token holds the ACL" as security decisions, not convenience ones.

field.label: Enable Read-Only SQL Tool
field.comment: Default: No. Setting this to Yes grants read access to most of this store's database to any MCP token whose admin role holds the Tool: Run Read-Only SQL Query ACL resource — customer records, addresses, order and payment metadata, quotes, and configuration values included. Queries are restricted to a single read-only SELECT and a deny-list blocks the most sensitive tables, but everything else is readable. Only enable this if you intend to give those token holders that level of access, and keep the ACL resource off every role that does not need it.

field.label: Default Row Limit
field.comment: Row cap applied when a query does not ask for one. Keeping this small limits how much data a single careless or hostile call can extract, and how much of it lands in the MCP audit log. Default 100.

field.label: Maximum Row Limit
field.comment: Hard ceiling a caller can never exceed, however large a limit it requests. This is the bulk-exfiltration brake — raising it directly raises how many rows one call can pull out of the store. Default 1000.

field.label: Statement Timeout (seconds)
field.comment: Server-side time budget per query. This is the denial-of-service brake: without it a single unindexed join can pin a database thread and starve the storefront. Raise it only if you accept that risk. Default 10.

field.label: Additional Denied Tables
field.comment:
One table name per line, added to the module's built-in deny-list. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.

Use this to protect data the built-in list cannot know about — custom tables holding credentials, API keys, tokens, or regulated customer data. Entries here only ever add restrictions; they cannot re-open a table the module already denies.
